plants.description: Ancient giant tree that thrives in dry, hot savannas. Some specimens are over 2,000 years old. Chapman's Baobab in the Makgadikgadi Pans was a famous landmark used as a beacon by early explorers.
plants.cultural_relevance: Known as the 'Tree of Life', of immense cultural and spiritual significance. Site for community gatherings, storytelling, and worship. Highly nutritious fruit (rich in Vitamin C) used in traditional dishes. Every part of the tree—bark for rope, leaves for medicine—is utilized. Symbol of resilience and life.

plants.description: Dominant tree in northern Botswana, covering vast areas. Thrives in hot, low-lying areas with poor, alkaline soils. Often forms dense pure stands known as 'mopane woodland'.
plants.cultural_relevance: Cornerstone of local livelihoods. Wood is hard, dense, termite-resistant—used for building homes, storage bins, livestock fences, and firewood. Host plant for the mopane worm, a protein-rich caterpillar that is a highly valued and economically important food source.
uses: Medicinal: leaves for fever, bark for diarrhea, wounds, stomach and tooth aches

plants.description: Extremely drought-resistant tree, often grows in association with termite mounds that provide moisture and nutrients in arid soil. Light-colored bark reflects sunlight.
plants.cultural_relevance: Vital resource in the Kalahari. Roots can be pounded to make porridge and a coffee substitute. Berries are used as a relish and have preservative qualities. A true survival tree.
uses: Roots for porridge and coffee substitute

plants.description: One of the most spectacular trees of the Okavango Delta, growing near permanent water sources. Massive, deeply fluted trunk can reach 20 meters high; natural holes shelter reptiles, rodents, and warthogs.
plants.cultural_relevance: Well-known landmark in the delta. Sweet, fig-like fruits are eaten by humans and animals. The strong, buttressed trunk is impossible for an elephant to uproot.

plants.description: Impressive tree found along permanent watercourses, growing over 25 meters tall, often on termite colonies. Straight trunk and dark-green crown.
plants.cultural_relevance: Famous for use in crafting mokoros (traditional dugout canoes). High-sugar-content fruit is a favorite of jackals, elephants, and many other animals.

plants.description: Grows in open woodland, floodplains, and along riverbanks. Tall, bare stem up to 20 meters high.
plants.cultural_relevance: Arguably the most culturally significant plant in northern Botswana. For centuries part of the Wayeyi culture. Leaves used for basket weaving—major income source in the northwest. Produces sweet, orange fruit called gau, highly sought after. Sap used to make palm wine (motjema or motsema).

plants.description: A shrub or small tree found in the deep sands of the Kalahari. Hardy species that thrives in arid conditions.
plants.cultural_relevance: Its beautiful white flowers make it a notable sight in an otherwise stark landscape.

plants.description: Dominates the classic Kalahari environment. Identified by the silvery sheen on its blue-grey leaves, a characteristic that helps reflect harsh sunlight and conserve water.
plants.cultural_relevance: An iconic tree of the Kalahari.

plants.description: One of the most common woody species in Botswana, drought-resistant, often grows in sandy soils.
plants.cultural_relevance: Wood highly prized for its density; used for high-quality firewood and charcoal.

plants.description: Common shrub in savanna and bushveld areas.
plants.cultural_relevance: Staple in rural livelihoods. Berries are eaten as snacks. One of the most mentioned wild edible plants in traditional Tswana diets.
Notable for its fruit, which Tswana people use to make a very potent alcoholic brew, much stronger than beer made from grain.

plants.setswana_name: Mokolwane (also used for fan palm, but specifically Phoenix reclinata)
plants.description: Evergreen palm growing in dense stands, often with curving stems.
plants.cultural_relevance: Edible fruit mentioned in Tswana folklore.
Among the Tswana, dried parts are smoked or powdered and inhaled to relieve congestion and cough.
World-renowned for its anti-inflammatory and analgesic properties. Harvested in Ghanzi, Kgalagadi, and Kweneng districts for export to European markets.

plants.latin_name: Various, e.g., Nymphaea nouchali (Blue Water Lily)
regions: Okavango Delta permanent swamps and channels
plants.description: Spectacular flowers defining the Okavango waterways.
plants.cultural_relevance: Favorite subject for photographers; a defining feature of the delta.
